1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:intro}
3	
4	The text on which large language models are trained increasingly contains their own outputs.
5	As synthetic content proliferates across the web, a recursive loop emerges: models trained on web corpora ingest text generated by earlier models, and their outputs feed into the next generation's training data \cite{shumailov2024_nature,alemohammad2024_mad}.
6	This model$\to$data$\to$model cycle is no longer hypothetical; it is already occurring in the wild. Yet whether the recursive generation depth of a text can be estimated from its statistical properties remains unstudied, a question that matters because first-generation synthetic text may be benign or even beneficial for training, while deeply recursive text drives the distributional collapse that degrades model quality \cite{dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails}.
7	We study this question under \emph{controlled full-replacement chains}, where each generation fully replaces the prior training set, isolating the depth variable. Real-world contamination typically involves partial mixing (accumulation), where synthetic and human data co-exist at unknown proportions; the full-replacement setting provides an upper bound on depth signal strength, and we discuss implications for accumulation settings in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
8	
9	Existing tools address adjacent but distinct problems.
10	Binary detectors such as Binoculars \cite{binoculars2024}, Fast-DetectGPT \cite{fast_detectgpt2024}, and DivEye \cite{diveye2026} classify text as human-written or machine-generated, collapsing all depths $d \geq 1$ into a single category.
11	Watermarking \cite{kirchenbauer2023_watermark} requires proactive embedding and cannot be applied retroactively.
12	The model collapse literature \cite{shumailov2024_nature,dohmatob2024_tale_of_tails} assumes depth is known a priori; \citet{drayson2025_detection_prevents_collapse} filter synthetic data via binary detection without distinguishing depths.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
3	We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification, constructing a 180K-passage benchmark spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement recursive chains at the 1--1.5B scale.
4	A Random Forest over statistical features dominated by the perplexity tail family achieves 69--86\% across nine model--strategy cells; convergence of RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM confirms that discriminative signal resides in perplexity distributional statistics, as independently confirmed by Binoculars feature convergence (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%, $p{>}0.05$).
5	Excluding the trivially separable human-written class (d0 recall ${>}$97\%), d1--d3 balanced accuracy ranges from 59\% to 82\%.
6	Cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\% (d1--d3: 45.9\%); the gap reveals that decoding strategies induce structurally distinct degradation trajectories, formalized via the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}4$ for all three families); preliminary 14B observations show above-chance accuracy (mean 50.8\%, $2{\times}$ chance) but $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$, indicating adjacent-depth discrimination does not survive the scale transition.
7	Perturbation-based and membership inference baselines (29--33\%) fall far below our pipeline; cross-perplexity features (Binoculars) converge to matching performance (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%), and merging both feature sets yields 82.6\%, decomposing the depth signal into perplexity displacement, distributional shape, and cross-model divergence channels.
8	\end{abstract}

5	The atlas spans $3 \times 3 = 9$ model--strategy cells at the 1--1.5B parameter scale, evaluated at depths $d \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, with depth extensions to $d{=}5$ for cross-model EDD validation (\S\ref{sec:atlas:edd}).

\item \textbf{Task formalization and benchmark.} We define recursive generation depth estimation as ordinal classification, introduce the EDD metric, and construct a 180K-sample benchmark ($3$ model families $\times$ $3$ decoding strategies $\times$ $4$ depths).

    \item \textbf{Depth Degradation Atlas.} The perplexity tail feature family dominates depth discrimination across all 9 cells; $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}4$ for all three families, validated by 5-class (d0--d4) extension (71--80\%); at $T{=}0.75$, Pythia achieves $p{=}0.001$ with graded confidence across families.

    \item \textbf{Generalization and cross-strategy analysis.} Cross-model LOO 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, single-cell prompted 69.5\%, preliminary cross-scale at 7--14B (mean 50.8\% at 14B but $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$, 60--70\% at 7--8B; \S\ref{sec:gen:crossscale}). We identify a structural barrier in cross-strategy transfer (59.1\%, d1--d3: 45.9\%): decoding strategies induce qualitatively distinct degradation trajectories, with d1/d2 boundary inversion under strategy mismatch.

    \item \textbf{Feature convergence analysis.} Independent cross-perplexity features (Binoculars) converge to matching ordinal accuracy (78.1\% vs.\ our 78.4\%); merging both feature sets yields 82.6\%, decomposing the depth signal into three channels: perplexity displacement (97\% of the full pipeline's accuracy), distributional shape (+2.5\,pp), and cross-model divergence (+4.2\,pp).
\end{itemize}

\begin{abstract}
As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification, constructing a 180K-passage benchmark spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement recursive chains at the 1--1.5B scale.
A Random Forest over statistical features dominated by the perplexity tail family achieves 69--86\% across nine model--strategy cells; convergence of RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM confirms that discriminative signal resides in perplexity distributional statistics, as independently confirmed by Binoculars feature convergence (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%, $p{>}0.05$).
Excluding the trivially separable human-written class (d0 recall ${>}$97\%), d1--d3 balanced accuracy ranges from 59\% to 82\%.
Cross-model transfer reaches 66.4\% (d1--d3: 55.4\%), cross-domain arXiv 74.1\%, and cross-strategy transfer 59.1\% (d1--d3: 45.9\%); the gap reveals that decoding strategies induce structurally distinct degradation trajectories, formalized via the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} (EDD) metric ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}4$ for all three families); preliminary 14B observations show above-chance accuracy (mean 50.8\%, $2{\times}$ chance) but $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$, indicating adjacent-depth discrimination does not survive the scale transition.
Perturbation-based and membership inference baselines (29--33\%) fall far below our pipeline; cross-perplexity features (Binoculars) converge to matching performance (78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%), and merging both feature sets yields 82.6\%, decomposing the depth signal into perplexity displacement, distributional shape, and cross-model divergence channels.
\end{abstract}
tool_args.new_text:
\begin{abstract}
As language models increasingly train on web text containing their own outputs, a recursive model$\to$data$\to$model loop arises, yet no method estimates how many such iterations a text has undergone.
We formalize \emph{recursive generation depth estimation} as ordinal classification and construct a 180K-passage benchmark spanning three model families, three decoding strategies, and four depths under controlled full-replacement chains at the 1--1.5B parameter scale.
A lightweight pipeline---19 statistical features dominated by perplexity tail statistics, classified by Random Forest---achieves d1--d3 balanced accuracy of 59--82\% across nine model--strategy cells, with the \emph{Effective Discriminable Depth} ($\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}$) reaching 4 for all three families.
Three findings emerge: (1)~depth signal concentrates in perplexity distribution tail statistics, confirmed by classifier convergence and independent cross-perplexity features (Binoculars, 78.1\% vs.\ 78.4\%); (2)~decoding strategy affects cross-condition transfer more than model architecture (d1--d3: 45.9\% cross-strategy vs.\ 55.4\% cross-model), revealing structurally distinct degradation trajectories; (3)~signal attenuates with scale---at 14B, $\mathrm{EDD}_{0.70}{=}0$ though accuracy remains $2{\times}$ chance.
Perturbation-based and membership-inference baselines (29--33\%) confirm that binary detection scores lack ordinal depth resolution.
\end{abstract}

**任务 1 [CRITICAL]: 扩展 Discussion (§6)**
当前 `discussion.tex` 仅 6 行（3 句话），对于这个体量的实证论文严重不足。需要扩展到 0.5-0.75 页（约 15-25 行 LaTeX），覆盖以下四个方向：

(a) **Depth-graduated curation 的实际含义**：当前 downstream curation PoC 是 negative（plan_013），但结果展示了 data efficiency story（44% 数据 ≈ 全量 PPL），同时 RF 筛选显著优于 random（p<0.002）。讨论 depth estimation 作为 data auditing 工具的实际路径：不追求直接过滤训练集，而是用于标记数据来源、监控 corpus 健康度、为 scaling law 研究提供 depth-stratified 分析。

(b) **Multi-channel depth encoding**：4 种 importance measure（Gini/SHAP/permutation/CPI, Kendall's W=0.90）收敛 + Binoculars 11-feature 独立路径达到统计不可区分准确率（78.1% vs 78.4%）→ depth signal 是 distributional property 而非 method artifact。不同特征子集（perplexity tail vs entropy vs lexical）捕获互补信号（merged 30-feat 82.6%），说明 recursive generation 在多个统计通道留下指纹。

(c) **Strategy effect > model effect (9.3pp vs 7.2pp)**：对实际部署的含义 -- auditing pipeline 必须考虑 decoding configuration。联系到 two-stage pipeline 的设计动机。与 Schaeffer et al. (2025) "operationally precise metrics" 的呼应：depth estimation 需要在操作参数（strategy, scale, reference model）下精确量化而非笼统声称。

(d) **Scale-dependent signal attenuation**：14B 结果明确框架为 "signal 存在但衰减" 的证据（consistent with tail-narrowing theory of Dohmatob et al. 2024），而非 "method 在 14B 有效"。reference mismatch 占 ~7pp 意味着 scale-matched reference model 可能恢复部分信号 → future work。

**页面约束**：Discussion 在 page 8 后半段。Limitations 不计入 8 页限制，所以可以把 Limitations 推到 page 9。但 Discussion 作为 §6 属于主文，必须在 page 8 内结束。当前 Limitations 在 page 8 占了 ~0.3 页空间，把这些空间让给 Discussion。

tool_args.new_text:
Cross-strategy transfer reveals a structural barrier: d1--d3 balanced accuracy drops to 45.9\% (four-class: 59.1\%), 7\,pp below cross-model transfer (Table~\ref{tab:cross_strategy}).
To address this, we design a two-stage pipeline: Stage~1 trains a 3-class strategy classifier on the same 19 features (57.8\% accuracy, chance = 33\%), then Stage~2 routes each sample to the strategy-conditioned depth classifier.
The pipeline achieves 70.5\% four-class accuracy ($+$11.5\,pp over the na\"ive LOO baseline of 59.1\%); oracle routing yields 78.3\%, so the 7.8\,pp gap is attributable to strategy misidentification.
Strategy identification is a tractable subproblem: even imperfect routing already recovers most of the within-strategy performance, and a 31.5\,pp d1--d3 gap between correct and incorrect routing confirms feature-space misalignment as the root cause (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).
Our depth estimation claims therefore hold most strongly within-strategy or when the decoding configuration is known.
